chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Ḥarīz: concerning

Wudu (ablution) dries. He said: I said, “Then if the first part dries before I wash that which comes after it?” He said, “Whether it dries or does not dry, wash what remains.” I said, “And likewise ghusl (ritual bath) of janabah?” He said, “It is at that same level, and begin with the head, then pour water over the rest of your body.” I said, “Even if it is after part of a day?” He said, “Yes.”

Thus, the correct understanding of this report is that if the one performing wudu (ablution) has not interrupted his wudu (ablution), and it is only dried by strong wind or intense heat, then in that case repeating it is not obligatory upon him. But whenever he interrupts the wudu (ablution), and then what he had washed dries, repeating it becomes obligatory upon him, as we have explained.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: Likewise, if he forgets to wipe his head and then remembers while there is still moisture from the wudu (ablution) in his hand, then he should wipe his head and his feet with that. And if he forgets to wipe his feet, then he should wipe them when he remembers with the moisture of his wudu (ablution) from his hand. If there is no moisture in his hand, but there is some in his beard or on his eyebrow, he should take from it whatever moistens the tips of his fingers and wipe his head and the upper part of his feet with it, even if it is little. But if he remembers what he forgot after his wudu (ablution) has dried and nothing of its moisture remains, then he should begin the wudu (ablution) anew from its beginning.

key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before salat (prayer)
key_terms.بَلَلٌ: remaining moisture used for wiping in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.جَفَّ: dried; referring to the loss of wetness between acts of purification
key_terms.ظَاهِرَ قَدَمَيْهِ: the upper part of his feet, the place of wiping in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.غُسْلُ الْجَنَابَةِ: ghusl (ritual bath) performed due to janabah
key_terms.فَلْيَسْتَأْنِفِ: let him recommence; meaning to restart the wudu (ablution) from the beginning
key_terms.لِحْيَتِهِ: his beard; a place from which remaining moisture may be taken
key_terms.مَسْحَ: wiping; the prescribed act over the head and feet in wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: If parts of wudu (ablution) dry before completion, must the wudu (ablution) be repeated?
ai.summary: This report discusses the legal rulings of continuity in wudu (ablution) and ghusl (ritual bath), clarifying when drying does and does not invalidate the process. It also explains the ruling for one who forgets the wiping of the head or feet, emphasizing the use of remaining moisture from wudu (ablution) and the need to restart if all moisture has completely dried after interruption.
